item.title: These workers help train robots who could one day steal their jobs
item.description: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

item.title: VIDEO: The skincare sample is free. What happens next can cost thousands
item.description: For years, customers have complained of aggressive sales tactics and charges at mall skincare stores. NPR investigated the business that connects many of them.

item.title: What to know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks to Dr. Otis Brawley, an oncologist at Johns Hopkins University, about the Pope's lung cancer diagnosis.

item.title: Writer Yiyun Li lost both of her sons. When words fell short, she turned to music
item.description: Li won a Pulitzer for her memoir about the suicides of her two sons. In her new novel, Music Against the Night, she writes about two young prodigies in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

item.title: Sauna research gathers steam
item.description: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.

item.title: Here's what to know if you're unsure about your measles immunity status
item.description: Vaccination is the best way to protect yourself against measles. For most adults, one shot of the MMR is considered enough protection. But there are certain situations that call for a second dose.
item.content:encoded: Vaccination is the best way to protect yourself against measles. For most adults, one shot of the MMR is considered enough protection. But there are certain situations that call for a second dose.

item.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
item.description: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.

item.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
item.description: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.

item.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
item.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

item.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
item.description: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.
